facts.title: Two-step labelling on NORMAL Clef (:8018) vs normal-mode answers on frozen-test stories (comparison only). Pre-registered config (threshold 0.20, meta questions in the 88-question screen call), n=294: readings F1 0.967 (recall .935, precision 1.0), identical reading set 97.6%, gate agreement 0.82 (FAIL vs 0.97: meta answers shift when grouped 88-per-call), place tags and country 100%, 24.5 stories/min (FAIL vs 28; normal mode 4 workers ~12.6-14/min = ~1.8x). ONE alternative (meta questions answered in their normal battery blocks, same requests as the full battery, threshold 0.20), n=147: readings F1 0.989, identical sets 99.3%, gate 1.00, place and country 100%, 24.0 stories/min, 4.98 attribute requests/story vs 17. Bars F1>=0.95 and gate>=0.97 pass in the alternative; speed >=28 fails in both (prediction R-0171).

Fast mode (NVFP4 two-step v2) vs normal-mode Clef Q4 on 300 frozen-test stories: readings agree F1 0.82 (recall 0.76 / precision 0.90), per-story identical set 88%, gate 72%; speed 82 stories/min (220 s). Bridge rule (<90% reading agreement): do not train on fast-mode labels; the two quantisations differ in answers (worst keys news_overload|down, trust_institutions|down). The record has no place/country/expected/severity.

Round 4 diagnosis (n=2,000 test, round-3 model): EXPECTED 0.59 = head limit, not threshold: with Clef's own reported set and allowed domains the best set match is only 0.646; model e| ranks well vs Clef raw e| (mean AUC .857, 80% of dials >=.8) but a global/per-key cut on tune rows gives no gain (tune set match .63 at cut .5-.6; F1-optimal per-key cuts made it worse, 0.53). CONDITIONS: ceiling of the head is TPR .25 at FPR .001 with the best possible pooled cut (median 5 Clef positives per key in 2,000 stories, 10 keys >=20): data-limited; Clef-only tuned cuts give TPR .24 at FPR .002. COUNTRY 0.8905: 40% of errors are the global class (acc .70; global<->usa/gbr confusions), region step wrong 8.3% vs country step 2.7%; rare countries are NOT the cause (0-19 train: 8 test stories); a bias on the global probability changes nothing (confident). GATE: Jev rows agree with Clef 77%.

Round 1b (Kaggle bitmob-mh-r1e: 15 epochs, lr 5e-5, same 1,097 Clef rows) vs round 1 on the same 789 Clef-labelled test stories: gate 0.61->0.70, topics domains AP>=.7 0%->27% (1.06 vs Clef 1.76 topics/story), country 0.31->0.76, expected 0.55->0.59, severity 0.62->0.73, conditions TPR 0.00 (no reading fires at the cuts; FPR 0). 0 of 6 rows pass

rounds_detail.tried: Cycle 2: a bigger reader (e5-large-v2, 3.4 times the size) trained on all 19,192 stories on both Kaggle GPUs for 38 minutes (10 passes).
rounds_detail.lesson: Bigger did not help the hardest step: conditions caught 24% (was 31%). It did help country (0.905, first pass). Reading a story costs 90 ms on the CPU (28 ms before) and 2 GB of memory. The conditions row is not a size problem; a hybrid is the realistic route.

P-0016.name: Should it read the story
P-0016.what: The engine first decides whether a story is worth reading at all (the gate). BitMob must make the same call as Clef.
P-0016.why: Round 3 reached 80% of Clef's calls. Jev's answers on this question only match Clef 77% of the time, and Clef's own answers are only 14% of the training stories.
P-0016.fix: Round 4 counts Clef's own answers twice as heavily (4 times instead of 2).

P-0017.name: Conditions
P-0017.what: What the story says is changing in the world (a dial going up or down). This is what moves the engine.
P-0017.why: More examples helped: the catch rate rose from 19% to 31% with 2,878 new Clef examples (41 of 78 conditions now have 50+). Still far from 90%.
P-0017.fix: Waiting on your decision: keep adding labels, or let Clef double-check the stories BitMob flags (hybrid).

P-0018.name: Topics
P-0018.what: Which subjects a story is about (several per story).
P-0018.fix: Passing. 6 topics still weak (religion, labour, sanctions...), watched each round.

P-0019.name: Country
P-0019.what: Which of 100 countries (or global) the story is about.
P-0019.why: Not rare countries (those are fine). 40% of the misses are stories Clef calls 'worldwide' that BitMob puts on the US or UK, or the other way round.
P-0019.fix: Clef's own answers weigh more (round 4); the 'worldwide' call is a judgement where Jev and Clef differ.

P-0020.name: Expected impact
P-0020.what: Which further changes the engine should expect next.
P-0020.why: The reader ranks the right changes well but misses Clef's exact list: even handed Clef's own choices of stories it reads and domains, it matches only 65%. Moving the cut-off did not help.
P-0020.fix: Heavier training on this answer and on Clef's own answers (round 4). If it stays flat, the bar needs a conversation.

P-0021.name: Severity
P-0021.what: How serious each change is (a level).
P-0021.fix: Passing on the full answer key (2,000 stories). Kept in check each round.

P-0023.what: Final check: run 300 stories through the engine with BitMob, and compare what comes out with Clef.
P-0023.why: Not run yet: it comes after the steps above pass.
